## Answers to the research questions (from the measured numbers)

* **RQ1** One pipeline (`engine.py`) runs geo-fencing and anomaly detection on every fix; 60 full runs succeeded at 100%, with alerts raised without any tourist action.
* **RQ2** Hybrid episode detection 97.9% (rules 76.2%, Isolation Forest 78.7%); false-alert walks 3.7%; window-level precision 1.00, recall 0.58.
* **RQ3** Salted-hash ID + proof-of-work hash chain + HMAC QR: 100% tamper detection, verification p95 5.08 ms, no raw passport stored.
* **RQ4** Server-side alert latency p95 11.5 ms. A measured manual-reporting baseline was NOT collected in Phase 1 (would need a user study), so no numeric comparison is claimed.
* **RQ5** False-alert walks: Isolation Forest alone 8.3% vs hybrid 3.7% (reduced). Mean delay: rules 276 s vs hybrid 281 s - the hybrid is NOT earlier on average; its benefit is higher COVERAGE (76.2% -> 97.9%), especially for lost/wandering behaviour that no rule describes.

Validation sweep: best F1 with <=5% false-alert walks = 0.74 at contamination 0.01, corroboration 60 m (see sweep.csv / fig_sweep.png).

## Honest limitations

* All numbers come from SYNTHETIC trajectories with simulated GPS noise; real-world performance may differ (real-dataset validation is future work).
* Alert latency is server-side processing only; SMS delivery delay is a simulated model unless Twilio credentials are configured.
* The ledger is a single-process simulation of a permissioned network (majority validation, proof-of-work), not a public blockchain with Byzantine fault tolerance.
* Ground truth for geo-fencing uses an independent planar implementation on the same coordinates; boundary points closer than 0.5 m are excluded.
